content.text: /ext:medcp Among elderly, what are the most frequent nutritional deficiency diagnoses?
I'll query the clinical records database. Let me first check the available tables.

This is an OMOP CDM database. Nutritional deficiency diagnoses live in `condition_occurrence`, joined to `concept` for names, and I'll restrict to elderly patients (age ≥ 65). Nutritional deficiencies map to SNOMED under the "Nutritional deficiency" hierarchy — I'll use `concept_ancestor` to capture that subtree.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT c.concept_id, c.concept_name
FROM omop.concept c
WHERE lower(c.concept_name) IN ('nutritional deficiency','nutritional deficiencies','deficiency of macronutrients','nutritional disorder')
  AND c.domain_id = 'Condition'
ORDER BY c.concept_name;

Let me use the `concept_ancestor` hierarchy to capture the whole nutritional-deficiency subtree, joined to elderly patients.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT c.concept_id, c.concept_name, COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id) AS n_patients, COUNT(*) AS n_diagnoses
FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = co.person_id
JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 4090739  -- Nutritional disorder
  AND (2026 - p.year_of_birth) >= 65
  AND c.standard_concept = 'S'
GROUP BY c.concept_id, c.concept_name
ORDER BY n_patients DESC
LIMIT 25;

JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = co.condition_concept_id

GROUP BY c.concept_id, c.concept_name
ORDER BY n_patients DESC;

The most frequent nutritional deficiency diagnoses among elderly patients (age ≥ 65) in this database, ranked by number of distinct patients:

| Rank | Diagnosis | Patients | Total diagnoses |
|------|-----------|---------:|----------------:|
| 1 | Vitamin D deficiency | 41,180 | 337,224 |
| 2 | Vitamin B deficiency | 10,702 | 77,396 |
| 3 | Undernutrition | 10,629 | 36,902 |
| 4 | Adult failure to thrive syndrome | 9,493 | 44,959 |
| 5 | Severe protein-calorie malnutrition | 8,980 | 28,469 |

| 9 | Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition | 3,651 | 10,553 |
| 10 | Nutritional deficiency disorder | 2,160 | 5,869 |

**Vitamin D deficiency dominates** — it affects nearly 4× more elderly patients than the next diagnosis, and its high diagnosis-to-patient ratio (~8) reflects repeated visits/coding. Vitamin deficiencies (D, B, B12) and protein-calorie malnutrition / failure-to-thrive are the dominant themes.

Notes on method: elderly defined as age ≥ 65 (2026 − year_of_birth); diagnoses drawn from `condition_occurrence` restricted to the SNOMED "Nutritional disorder" hierarchy via `concept_ancestor`, counting distinct patients. A couple of overload conditions (hemochromatosis, iron overload) fall in the same subtree but aren't deficiencies.
